claim: In [31i] (two thirds) the predeterminer is a nominal.
evidence_summary: Page 434: “Predeterminers expressing fractions have the form of NPs”, since half, quarter and third take determiners such as cardinals. Page 331 [10a] also gives an NP in this function.
finding: Call two thirds an NP. A nominal cannot contain the determiner two.
proposed_wording: In [i–ii] the predeterminer is respectively an NP and a noun
inference: Which category realizes the fused predeterminer in two thirds?

evidence.passage: §9.4, p. 419. “In [i–ii] the predeterminer is respectively a nominal and a noun”.
evidence.establishes: Two category labels for the same expression type.
evidence.note: Local source (working note, unpublished draft or local copy); not online.
